scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the experimental logging, reproducibility framework, and candor regarding protocol deviations are commendable, the paper's substantive evaluation of scientific quality rests entirely on uncalibrated external LLM reviewers without human expert corroboration across only five runs. Under conservative curation standards, the lack of independent ground truth or human calibration for paper quality warrants an uncertain verdict.

runs the study from its records before the agent revises the paper. Over 13 development runs,

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The headline quality claim rests on uncalibrated AI reviewers reading only the papers, with no human expert evaluation or calibration against human decisions, so workshop-level quality is not established.
The five-run sample with a single research model and no ablations cannot attribute outcomes to the question procedure, critic, or reviewer, leaving the central contribution underdetermined.

The post-hoc amendment counting the pilot after three results had been seen, and the post-hoc choice of PDF reviews as the main result after seeing Markdown reviews, introduce selection and reporting deviations that weaken the pre-registered evaluation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The external reviewers come from model families other than the research agent and were not involved in drafting or revision, and the in-loop reviewer re-ran the studies from records to verify reproducibility.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External AI reviews by Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder, which read only the final papers and scored them on six axes with workshop and main-track judgments.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The in-loop critic (GPT-6-astra) and in-loop reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5) shaped the papers through critique adoption and revision, and the system was developed over 13 runs with instruction changes informed by post-run assessments.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of full autonomy from formulation to write-up and strict re-computability are supported by run records and deterministic replay scripts. However, claims regarding scientific quality and impact remain weakly corroborated due to reliance on uncalibrated LLM judges.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The primary evaluation relies on in-loop AI reviewer re-execution and external AI reviews by two separate LLMs (Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder), which rate papers at workshop level but low in novelty and clarity. However, sample size is limited to five runs, no human expert evaluation or comparison against human baselines is provided, and the pre-registration protocol underwent a post-hoc amendment to include the pilot run.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Re-execution and reproducibility checks were verified independently through executable scripts from clean git tags, and external review signals came from distinct model families not involved in drafting.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External automated reviews across 6 rubric axes and overall acceptance ratings from Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly disclose protocol deviations (post-hoc counting of the pilot run), sample size limits (five runs, single research model family), lack of human evaluation, and the tendency of agents to converge on narrow open-data resources.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Deterministic checks on numerical consistency, solver logs, convergence records, and provenance run alongside the model-based rubric scoring, and the reported stage-level results are consistent with these independent checks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcomes are established by clean-replay evidence scored through deterministic checks and a GPT-5.6-sol rubric evaluator applied to regenerated artifacts.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The agent configurations are optimized through their model training and scaffold execution loops, with no access to the private reference workflow or rubric during task execution.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding current LLM limitations in paper-level cross-disciplinary reproduction are well aligned with and supported by the granular empirical results across the 930 evaluated outcomes.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation comprehensively tests 10 frontier model configurations across all 93 tasks, detailing stage-wise metrics across Modeling, Execution, and Validation. The experimental analysis convincingly highlights that while agents often achieve reasonable modeling/execution scores (~62%), full reproduction remains rare (leading model achieves only 13.98% full rate), with thorough diagnostic case studies illustrating failure modes.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Deterministic checks of numerical outputs, simulation logs, convergence criteria, and ground-truth physics/numerical consistency run independently alongside the model-based rubric scoring.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Replay-grounded evidence verification scored via deterministic checks and a frozen GPT-5.6-sol rubric evaluator operating on freshly regenerated simulation artifacts.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Frontier agent prompt instructions and tool scaffold execution loops operating under fixed reasoning settings and shell access without access to reference rubrics.

primary.limitations: The work openly documents its licensing restrictions (three tasks cannot distribute proprietary commercial environments directly), resource ceilings, fallback conventions for refusals, and reliance on an LLM judge for rubrics requiring domain interpretation alongside deterministic checks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing a two-stage task construction pipeline requiring reference implementation execution, clean replay, calibration with positive/negative controls, and independent expert reviews. The evaluation protocol isolates submissions in clean containers, enforces replay-grounded verification, and evaluates regenerated numerical artifacts using both deterministic checks and expert rubrics.
primary.quality_rationale: The benchmark addresses a significant gap in cross-domain scientific execution and reproduction for AI agents, presents a rigorous execution-and-replay verification framework, and provides extensive diagnostics and validation protocols.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces PAPERBENCHX, a curated benchmark of 93 paper-reproduction tasks across 12 scientific disciplines and 10 domain-native computing environments (e.g., HFSS, Meep, PySCF, Quantum ESPRESSO), evaluating whether frontier LLM agents can reconstruct and reproduce published scientific claims via clean replay and rubric-based evidence scoring.

We formalize each category as a rewriting rubric
(Table 1) and prompt GPT-5.4 mini to generate un-
derspecified query variants (see Appendix A.1 for
the prompts). To verify whether these variants re-
semble naturally occurring underspecified queries,
we conduct a Turing-style discrimination test (Tur-
ing, 1950). We first apply the rewriting procedure
to the clarified queries in our collected query pairs
from real users. We then pair each generated vari-
ant with its corresponding human-written initial
query and ask a separate model to identify which
query is AI-generated and which is human-written.
We repeat the test twice, shuffling the order
of the human-written and AI-generated queries
in each run. Across 486 generated variants de-
rived from 176 clarified queries, GPT-4o achieves
identification accuracies of 58% and 54%, respec-
tively, slightly higher than random guessing.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The clarification-behavior classifier was validated against human annotations on a 10% sample with Cohen's kappa of 0.92, and query variants received human validation, providing evaluator-independent checks on key measurement components.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by Gemini 3.1 Pro rubric and citation-support scoring, programmatic search-trajectory metrics, and GPT-5.4 mini classification of clarification behavior.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evaluated deep research agents and LLM judges are pre-existing systems used as frozen models; the paper performs no training, tuning, reward modeling, or adaptation against its evaluation metrics.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding drops in rubric alignment, preserved citation precision, limited DRA clarification awareness, and shifts in intermediate search dynamics are directly supported by paired experimental findings and detailed trajectory metrics.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation tests three deep research agents (DR Tulu-8B, GPT-5.4 with tools, and Tongyi-DR) across ResearchQA, ScholarQA-Bench, and DeepResearch Bench. It combines paired non-parametric statistical testing with Bonferroni correction for answer rubrics and human-validated automated categorization for clarification behaviors.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Because no agent or model was trained or tuned against the evaluation metrics, signal reuse is not applicable.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Automated rubric scoring and citation support evaluated by Gemini 3.1 Pro alongside programmatic search trajectory measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-existing, pre-trained deep research agents and LLMs evaluated as frozen systems without paper-level training, adaptation, or tuning loops.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including a predominant focus on English queries, evaluation restricted to agents with accessible intermediate trajectories, and lack of coverage for proprietary closed-source systems without exposed traces.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is grounded in qualitative coding of user reformulations and generates matched query variants verified via Turing-style model discrimination and author validation. Intermediate search trajectories are comprehensively analyzed using established operational metrics such as query drift, transition classifications, token provenance, and document novelty.
primary.quality_rationale: This study addresses an important gap in understanding the robustness of autonomous research agents under realistic, imperfect user prompts. The experimental design is rigorous, methodologically sound, transparently scoped, and thoroughly validated.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces UNDERSPEC-DR, an empirical evaluation framework based on 176 real user query reformulations to systematically evaluate how scope, terminology, and preference underspecification impact deep research agent performance and intermediate search trajectories across three open benchmarks.
